note: Starter lists and typical amounts for the Session (Phase 2.5, Batch 3). Which lines show follows the Profile's answers (engine/profile.js fieldsFor), not this file. Typical amounts are rough monthly guesses for a single adult in 2026, marked as guesses wherever they land; the client types over them. Made up, not anyone's real numbers. withdrawalChips: the withdrawal rates offered as one-tap chips on Goals (owner, 2026-10-28).

withdrawal.label: 5.2% with guardrails
withdrawal.source: Jonathan Guyton and William Klinger, Decision Rules and Maximum Initial Withdrawal Rates (Journal of Financial Planning, 2006)
withdrawal.note: Only with the guardrails in retirement: cut spending by 10% when the withdrawal rate climbs 20% above where it started, and raise it by 10% when it falls 20% below.

withdrawal.source: William Bengen, A Richer Retirement (2025): his updated safe rate, the same as the optimistic set
William Bengen, Determining Withdrawal Rates Using Historical Data (1994); the Trinity study (Cooley, Hubbard and Walz, 1998)
Morningstar, The State of Retirement Income (2024): a 30-year retirement
Early Retirement Now, Safe Withdrawal Rate series (2016 on): a 50 to 60 year retirement
Morningstar, The State of Retirement Income (2021)

typical.note: Typical monthly amounts for one adult, shown as typical and stored as a guess wherever they land. Each amount names the published table it should come from (sources below). The BLS, HUD and Census sites could not be reached when this was built (2026-10-27), so every number is still the earlier estimate, marked verify (QUESTIONS.md 124). Not anyone's real numbers.

rent.source: HUD Fair Market Rent, one bedroom (city: large metros; elsewhere: national median), cross-checked with Census ACS median gross rent (B25064)

pay-family.source: No published average: Eli's guess for rent paid to family

mortgage.source: Census ACS median monthly owner costs with a mortgage (B25088)

property-tax.source: Census ACS median real estate taxes paid (B25103), a year divided by 12
